transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Tom Reynolds (CedarEdge - Head Proc), Aisha Khan (CISO), Liam Murphy (VP Eng), Sofia Martinez (Legal)

Summary: Final procurement/legal review of MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing approval path, and vendor onboarding milestones. Agreement on a small set of redlines, next steps to exchange redlined documents, and a pilot/onboarding kickoff date contingent on signatures.

[00:00] Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, um, with a quick agenda - legal review, SLA items, pricing approvals, and onboarding timeline. Priya will cover technical SLAs and runbook bits after I run through the commercial items.
[00:18] Tom Reynolds: Sounds good. We have Sofia from legal and Aisha from security on the line to pick through the MSA/DPA items. Liam's here for the integration questions.
[00:28] Jordan Blake: Great, quick check - does everyone have the latest MSA/DPA I sent yesterday? I see a thumbs from Sofia, okay.
[00:36] Sofia Martinez: Yes we have it, small caveat that we forwarded a couple of redlines in the DPA around breach notification timing and subprocessor disclosure.
[00:49] Priya Sharma: Noted. From a tech side, we usually do 72-hour initial notice on incidents but we can surface full forensics in parallel - we'll align on language.
[01:05] Aisha Khan: For us, 72 is borderline — we'd prefer 48 for critical data incidents. Also need clarity around KMS — we need a customer-managed KMS option and proof of HSM for key storage.
[01:22] Jordan Blake: We do offer customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and HSM-backed options for our Private deployments. For Hosted API the standard is Redwood-managed KMS with bring-your-own-key offered on Dedicated/Private — we'll flag that in the DPA.
[01:40] Liam Murphy: Quick question on data residency — we need EU-only processing for the pilot, can that be enforced?
[01:49] Priya Sharma: Yes, we can route to region-specific capacity. For Dedicated or Private customers you can pin region, for Hosted we provide EU data centers and an option to force routing to EU-only — we'll put that in the SOW.
[02:05] Tom Reynolds: On SLA, finance needs the uptime SLA and credits spelled out. What are you proposing?
[02:12] Jordan Blake: Standard proposal in the quote is 99.95% uptime with credits tiered: 99.9-99.95 small credit, <99.9 larger. Priya can walk through what that corresponds to technically.
[02:22] Priya Sharma: Right, so 99.95% is across the control plane and model serving for Dedicated. For Hosted there's a different baseline but we can put 99.9 guaranteed for the Hosted plan with fallbacks. Also note we include automatic failover to a warm standby region for critical endpoints to meet the SLOs.
[02:40] Sofia Martinez: Are there any termination for convenience fees? We prefer a 30-day exit option for pilot customers.
[02:47] Jordan Blake: For pilots we usually allow 30-day termination. For annual committed Dedicated capacity there are penalties; those are negotiable in the SOW.
[02:59] Aisha Khan: Security questionnaire — we completed the initial one, but we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and ISO attestation. Do you have an auditor report?
[03:10] Jordan Blake: Yes, we can provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 attestation. I'll include the security pack link.
[03:18] Tom Reynolds: Great. On pricing approvals: procurement needs the final approved quote to route for budget sign-off. Any outstanding pricing items?
[03:26] Jordan Blake: The main open is the Dedicated reservation tier vs hosted concurrency pricing. We've proposed a 12-month reserved pool with a blended per-token discount. There's an option to start pilot on Hosted with converted credits applied to Dedicated commit if they decide to convert.
[03:41] Liam Murphy: Is there a minimum commit? We're trying to avoid upfront heavy spend, prefer to test and then commit.
[03:46] Jordan Blake: We can do a small committed tier as a pilot bridge — e.g., 2 GPUs reserved for three months with option to expand — that'll give predictability and smoother SLA.
[03:55] Sofia Martinez: Legal wants clear language on data deletion after termination — 30 days plus certification of deletion?
[04:03] Priya Sharma: We provide data deletion within 30 days and can provide a deletion certificate. For Private deployments if you host on your infra, retention policies are customer-controlled.
[04:16] Aisha Khan: Also need export controls and subprocessors list — we need name and location of major subprocessors.
[04:24] Jordan Blake: We'll include an updated subprocessors list and a commitment to notify of any changes.
[04:31] [05:00] Speaker 2: (mumble) sorry, what was the SL...
[05:03] Priya Sharma: —the SLA tiers I mentioned earlier, 99.95 for Dedicated, 99.9 for Hosted, and credits escalate based on minutes of downtime. We can share the SLA workbook which maps the credit math.
[05:16] Tom Reynolds: Can you confirm response times for P1 incidents — our ops team wants 30-minute acknowledgement and 4-hour remediation target?
[05:24] Priya Sharma: We can commit to 30-minute acknowledgement and aim for 4-hour initial remediation for critical incidents on Dedicated with a priority support add-on. For Hosted, we do 1-hour acknowledgement generally. The priority add-on is included in our enterprise package.
[05:40] Aisha Khan: For encryption in-transit and at-rest — any customer-managed key option for Hosted APIs?
[05:47] Jordan Blake: BYOK is available on Dedicated/Private. For Hosted APIs we can discuss a managed BYOK path with additional compliance review; we'll add that as an appendix.
[05:58] Liam Murphy: On the onboarding timeline — if legal signs by Dec 20, when can we start the pilot?
[06:05] Jordan Blake: Realistically, pilot kickoff the first week of January — dependencies: signed MSA/DPA, PO for pilot credit, and scheduling the onboarding session. So Jan 4 or Jan 6 is doable.
[06:17] Sofia Martinez: That's tight for us but doable if internal approvals run on schedule. We'll aim to have legal decision by the 18th like Tom said.
[06:25] Jordan Blake: Cool. Pricing approvals — I'll add a formal quote that reflects the blended pricing and deposit terms. Tom, will you be the procurement owner to route that?
[06:33] Tom Reynolds: Yes I'll route. I'll need line items for pilot and committed capacity separate. Also need billing contact and invoice cadence.
[06:40] Jordan Blake: We'll send monthly invoices for the pilot, and for committed Reserved it's monthly billed against the commit. Billing contact noted.
[06:47] Priya Sharma: I'll dive into the technical specifics: latency SLOs, model variants, and fallback behavior.
[06:53] [07:00] Priya Sharma: For the pilot use-case you described — customer-facing summarization and search — we'll recommend a mid-sized open model quantized to int8 on Dedicated. Expected p95 latency for 512 tokens is ~220ms with batching off for low latency. With batching/kv-cache optimizations we can lower cost without hurting p95 too much.
[07:24] Liam Murphy: That latency estimate is helpful. Our SLAs are end-to-end, do you include network variability in those p95 numbers?
[07:31] Priya Sharma: The numbers are for server-side processing only. We'll include guidance for client-side/network e2e considerations in the runbook. For strict e2e SLOs we recommend edge routing and a regional endpoint pinned to EU for your region.
[07:46] Aisha Khan: Do you offer pen test reports or third-party validation? We need to include that in security assessment.
[07:52] Jordan Blake: Yes, we have pen test summaries and can coordinate a customer-specific assessment if needed — usually part of the enterprise onboarding scope.
[07:59] Sofia Martinez: Regarding indemnity clauses, we have a few redlines. Can Redwood accept the proposed limitation cap tied to fees?
[08:07] Jordan Blake: We typically tie liability caps to a multiple of fees (often 1x or 2x annual fees depending on the clause). We can discuss specifics in redline exchange.
[08:18] Tom Reynolds: On the SSO side — SAML + SCIM provisioning is required. Is that supported?
[08:23] Priya Sharma: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported out of the box for enterprise customers. We'll provide a SAML setup guide in the onboarding packet.
[08:33] Liam Murphy: For the pilot, do we get production-grade observability? We need per-route latency and token-level cost breakdowns for the pilot.
[08:41] Priya Sharma: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level billing, and tracing hooks — we can give access to a sandbox console for the pilot.
[08:53] Sofia Martinez: Back to DPA — the subprocessors clause: we'd like 30 days notice for new subprocessors, can you do that?
[09:00] Jordan Blake: Standard is 30 days for major subprocessors; we'll confirm that in the DPA.
[09:08] [09:30] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) one sec, Tom did you say finance approval timeline?
[09:35] Tom Reynolds: We're aiming for internal budget approval by Dec 18. Procurement will then route the PO.
[09:41] Jordan Blake: Okay we'll align timelines to that.
[09:45] Priya Sharma: Technical note — for the pilot we'd like to run a 72-hour benchmark to validate latency and cost for your workload. We'll include a benchmark plan in the runbook.
[09:56] Liam Murphy: That benchmark should match our production prompt mix, we'll send sample traffic and prompt set.
[10:01] Priya Sharma: Perfect, please send that to me and I'll lay out the test parameters.
[10:05] Aisha Khan: On data deletion certification — can you also include logs retention policy and possibility to shorten retention for the pilot?
[10:13] Jordan Blake: Yes logs retention can be configured and shortened for pilot environments; we'll document that.
[10:20] Sofia Martinez: If you can send redlined MSA and DPA by Monday the 14th, we can aim to review and revert by the 18th.
[10:28] Jordan Blake: That's doable. We'll send redlines and updated SLA workbook and subprocessors list.
[10:33] Tom Reynolds: Great. For approvals I'll need the final quote and SOW attached to the MSA for sign-off.
[10:40] Jordan Blake: We'll attach the SOW and quote. Also I'll note the pilot-to-dedicated conversion credit language so finance can see it.
[10:48] Priya Sharma: I'll also include the onboarding runbook, SAML guide, and the pilot benchmark plan.
[10:54] Jordan Blake: Any last items?
[10:57] Liam Murphy: One more — what about fallback policies if you deprecate a model our app depends on? Is there a compatibility guarantee?
[11:05] Priya Sharma: We provide model variant compatibility guidance and automated fallback to compatible variants; we can add a compatibility SLA in the SOW for critical endpoints.
[11:16] Aisha Khan: Okay that helps.
[11:19] Jordan Blake: Alright I'll summarize next steps — send redlined MSA/DPA, SLA workbook, subprocessors list, onboarding runbook, and pricing quote by 2026-12-14. CedarEdge to review and revert by 2026-12-18. If signed, target onboarding kickoff the week of 2027-01-04.
[11:36] Sofia Martinez: Sounds good, we'll prioritize review.
[11:39] Tom Reynolds: Thanks everyone.
[11:41] Jordan Blake: Thanks all, talk soon.
